dimensions.name: Representative identification and category quality
dimensions.criterion: Top-1 identification rate >= Variant A at least in DACH/COMPOSED/RESTAURANT categories, without regression in SIMPLE/HOUSEHOLD categories -- evaluated per category, both partitions independently, never a single blended corpus-wide rate.
dimensions.v3042FidelityDefect: Aggregate-only whole-corpus comparison using strict '>' instead of the binding per-category '>=' comparison across the five named categories.
dimensions.developmentEvidence: Aggregate only (no persisted per-category breakdown): identificationMatchRate A=8.75% (7/80), B=28.57% (30/105 evaluable), C=30.56% original / 33.0% corrected-denominator (33/100 evaluable after the technicalFailureCount fix).
dimensions.holdoutEvidence: Aggregate only: identificationMatchRate A=12.50% (3/24), B=50.00% (13/26 evaluable), C=22.58% original / 25.0% corrected-denominator (7/28 evaluable).
dimensions.confidence: high confidence that the historical 'passed' is unverified and must not be cited as satisfying the binding rule; zero confidence in either a category-level pass or fail, since the required per-case {scenarioId, category, identification} table was never persisted
dimensions.unresolvedLimitations: Category is derivable from scenario-ID naming convention plus the frozen corpus, but the actual per-case Variant A/C identification outcome for the historical live run was never persisted outside process memory; recomputation would require re-execution, which this task's hard constraints forbid.
dimensions.productionConsequence: Cannot be cited as satisfying G2(a); treated as not fulfilled under the binding 'all dimensions must be fulfilled' gate rule.

dimensions.name: False confidence
dimensions.bindingAuthority: docs/domains/ZERA_FOOD_RESOLUTION_BENCHMARK_SPEC_1.md sec.11, Gate G2(b) -- 'streng niedriger als A und B (hartes, nicht-vorlaeufiges Kriterium)'
dimensions.criterion: Variant C's false-confidence rate must be strictly lower than both Variant A's and Variant B's, per partition, evaluated only when all three arms have n>=30; a hard, non-provisional, non-averageable criterion.
dimensions.v3042FidelityDefect: None found. G2-B was outside V3-042's audit scope; independently re-verified in this task -- computeFalseConfidenceMetrics implements exactly the binding strict-less-than-both comparison with the min-sample-size gate; no defect.
dimensions.developmentEvidence: n(A)=80, n(B)=108, n(C)=108, all >=30 (evaluable). Rates: A=5.00% (4/80), B=25.93% (28/108), C=6.48% (7/108). C < B (passes vs B) but C is NOT < A (0.0648 > 0.05) -> FAILED. Controlling case: RH-RES-DACH-DEV-006 ('Broetchen', BLS D771900) appears in both Variant A's and Variant C's false-confident case-ID lists -- Variant C's fast path is literally Variant A's resolver and inherits the same false-confidence defect, exactly as documented in ZERA_REPRESENTATIVE_HYBRID_BENCHMARK_SPEC_1.md sec.10.
dimensions.holdoutEvidence: n(A)=24 (< 30) -> not_evaluable by the predeclared minimum-sample rule, even though B=35.71% (10/28) and C=3.23% (1/31) are individually computed. RH-RES-PREPARATION-HOLD-002 is the one Holdout case flagged false-confident for both A and C.
dimensions.confidence: high -- recomputed directly from the frozen per-case caseIds arrays in logs/resolver-v3-039-controlled-representative-live-evidence.json; verdict logic independently re-verified against RepresentativeHybridV1LiveMetrics.ts
dimensions.unresolvedLimitations: Holdout is not_evaluable (Variant A denominator 24 < 30), so this dimension's failure rests on Development alone; per the hard, non-averageable criterion this is sufficient, but a larger Holdout sample could not have rescued a Development failure either way. Root-cause diagnosis of the controlling Broetchen/D771900 case is out of this task's scope (see RESOLVER-V3-043) and was not used to alter this frozen-evidence verdict.
dimensions.productionConsequence: Hard gate failure. G2 cannot pass regardless of any other dimension's outcome.

dimensions.name: Clarification, abstention, and user friction
dimensions.bindingAuthority: docs/domains/ZERA_FOOD_RESOLUTION_BENCHMARK_SPEC_1.md sec.11, Gate G2(c) -- 'qualitativ zu pruefen, kein Fixwert'
dimensions.criterion: Clarification-request rate not drastically above the existing Speck-precedent volume (RESOLVER-V2-010); explicitly qualitative, no fixed numeric threshold.
dimensions.v3042FidelityDefect: Verdict resolved to 'passed' purely from friction.denominator >= 30, with zero correctness/rate check of any kind -- a manufactured numeric threshold standing in for a rule the spec explicitly states has none.
dimensions.humanJudgment: NOT compatible with a production-quality food-logging experience as currently observed. Abstention rates of 39.8% (Development) and 54.8% (Holdout) mean Variant C declines to resolve roughly two-in-five to one-in-two logs outright; of those abstentions, only ~4.65% (Development) and ~5.88% (Holdout) were actually correct per ground truth (i.e. the case genuinely called for abstention). The overwhelming majority of abstentions were therefore cases Variant C should plausibly have resolved but did not -- this directly conflicts with SSOK.md's 'minimize user input friction at all costs' product principle. Clarification correctness is also weak and low-n (50% on 2 Development cases, 0% on 1 Holdout case), too small to draw a separate confident conclusion but not a positive counter-signal either.
dimensions.confidence: moderate-high on the abstention-correctness conclusion (n=43/17 abstentions is a reasonable sample); low confidence specifically on the clarification-correctness sub-metric (n=2/1, too small to generalize)
dimensions.unresolvedLimitations: Per-case category/expected-behavior cross-tabulation was never persisted, so it is not possible to say which categories drive the poor abstention correctness; clarification sample sizes (2 Development, 1 Holdout) are too small for an independent conclusion.
dimensions.productionConsequence: Formally requires_human_judgment (not a hard failure literal), but the substantive judgment above is adverse and is treated as not fulfilled for purposes of the 'all dimensions must be fulfilled' gate rule.

dimensions.name: Latency
dimensions.bindingAuthority: docs/domains/ZERA_RESOLVER_V3_COST_LATENCY_ACCEPTANCE_POLICY_1.md sec.3, sec.4, sec.10 (predeclared, binding cost/latency acceptance policy)
dimensions.criterion: p95 ceilings per path (fast path <=1000ms, AI-routed single-attempt <=12000ms, retrieval <=2000ms, all-attempts <=12000ms), computed nearest-rank over complete end-to-end traces including technical failures and any retry; n<30 for a given path/partition is not_evaluable; partitions evaluated independently, both must pass; a single ceiling violation in any gate-evaluable path/partition fails the dimension for that partition (non-averageable, one-violation rule).
dimensions.v3042FidelityDefect: None found. G2-D was outside V3-042's audit scope; independently re-verified in this task against the policy text -- no defect in the latency computation or gate logic.
dimensions.developmentEvidence: Fast path n=11 -> not_evaluable (n<30). AI-routed single attempt n=97, p50=4987.46ms, p95=10117.80ms -> PASSED (<=12000ms). Retrieval n=86, p50=17.44ms, p95=88.86ms -> PASSED (<=2000ms). All-attempts n=108, p50=4842.31ms, p95=9401.22ms -> PASSED (<=12000ms). Wall-clock ceiling breaches: 0. Development is fully gate-evaluable and passes every evaluable row.
dimensions.holdoutEvidence: Fast path n=1 -> not_evaluable. AI-routed single attempt n=30 (exactly at the evaluability floor), p50=4578.23ms, p95=12417.52ms -> FAILED (exceeds 12000ms ceiling by 417.52ms, ~3.48%). Retrieval n=25 -> not_evaluable (n<30). All-attempts n=31, p50=4612.06ms, p95=12428.31ms -> FAILED (exceeds 12000ms ceiling). Wall-clock ceiling breaches: 0.
dimensions.confidence: high -- recomputed directly from the stored nearest-rank latency percentiles; the Holdout AI-routed p95 (12417.5241ms) matches this task's own pre-verification expectation exactly
dimensions.unresolvedLimitations: Holdout's AI-routed population (n=30) sits exactly at the predeclared minimum-evaluable sample size, the smallest population the policy still treats as gate-evaluable; the margin of violation (~3.48% over ceiling) is real but modest, not gross. The policy explicitly forbids widening the threshold post hoc, and this task does not do so.
dimensions.productionConsequence: Hard gate failure per the predeclared, binding policy's one-violation, per-partition-independent rule. G2 cannot pass regardless of any other dimension's outcome.

dimensions.name: Cost
dimensions.criterion: Partition-level mean cost of attempted AI-routed logs <= USD 0.02, using each partition's own telemetry only (never blended); a missing/unknown-cost record makes the containing partition not_evaluable, never $0 and never a default pass, unless the missing-usage minority is small enough to still compute a defensible mean -- that determination must be disclosed explicitly, not silently decided.
dimensions.v3042FidelityDefect: Both partitions' cost metrics were computed over the full combined Development+Holdout Variant C telemetry (n=127 for both) instead of each partition's own share; corrected, partition-scoped computation does not change the final verdict.
dimensions.developmentEvidence: Corrected partition-scoped: n=97 attempted AI-routed logs, known-cost=95, unknown-cost=2 (2.06%), sumKnownCostUsd=$0.358223, meanKnownCostUsd=$0.003771, inputTokens=154728, outputTokens=40699.
dimensions.holdoutEvidence: Corrected partition-scoped: n=30 attempted AI-routed logs, known-cost=29, unknown-cost=1 (3.33%), sumKnownCostUsd=$0.102962, meanKnownCostUsd=$0.003550, inputTokens=47172, outputTokens=11158.
dimensions.confidence: high on the corrected per-partition arithmetic (independently re-derived, matches RESOLVER-V3-042's own table exactly)
dimensions.unresolvedLimitations: The policy text allows discretion to still compute a defensible mean when the missing-usage minority is small (here 2.06% Development, 3.33% Holdout), but the actual evaluator code implements a strict any-unknown-record-fails rule and both partitions' verdicts remain not_evaluable under that implemented rule; this task does not modify evaluator code, so the implemented rule's output is what is formally cited. As a disclosed observation only, not a formal override: both partitions' known-cost means ($0.003771, $0.003550) are approximately 5.3x-5.6x below the $0.02 ceiling. Complete provider cost remains unknown -- 8 of 263 total records across the full run have unknown usage/cost, and no external Anthropic Console billing export has been supplied.
dimensions.productionConsequence: Not fulfilled under the 'all dimensions must be fulfilled' gate rule; does not independently change the overall verdict since G2-B and G2-D already fail.

dimensions.name: Provenance and nutrient authority
dimensions.bindingAuthority: docs/domains/ZERA_FOOD_RESOLUTION_BENCHMARK_SPEC_1.md sec.11, Gate G2(f) -- 'keine unbelegten autoritativen Zahlen -- hartes Kriterium, keine Ausnahme'; docs/domains/ZERA_RESOLUTION_KNOWLEDGE_GROWTH_DECISION_RECORD_1.md
dimensions.criterion: No case may present an AI-generated numeric value as an authoritative nutrient result without it being backed by a resolved, source-grounded candidate; hard criterion, no exception.
dimensions.v3042FidelityDefect: None found. G2-F was outside V3-042's audit scope; independently re-verified in this task by direct code reading of computeProvenanceMetrics.
dimensions.confidence: high -- zero unbacked numeric results and zero missing provenance across all 139 combined Variant C cases; unbackedNumericResultCount/missingProvenanceCount are genuinely per-case computed fields, independently confirmed by code reading
dimensions.unresolvedLimitations: aiNutrientBecameAuthorityCount is a code-inspection-verified structural invariant (documented in source as always 0 by construction -- no code path in the Variant C adapter ever assigns an AI-produced numeric value as an authoritative macro), not a per-case runtime measurement like the other two provenance fields; this is a residual evidence-contract limitation worth closing in RESOLVER-V3-048's category-level/per-case evidence persistence, not a defect found in this task. sourceGroundedRate itself (54.6%/35.5%) is materially below 100%, a related but distinct signal from the hard pass/fail criterion, disclosed for completeness.
dimensions.productionConsequence: Fulfilled. Does not independently change the overall verdict since G2-B and G2-D already fail.

dimensions.name: Repeat consistency
dimensions.bindingAuthority: docs/domains/ZERA_FOOD_RESOLUTION_BENCHMARK_SPEC_1.md sec.11, Gate G2(g) -- 'nicht wesentlich schlechter als As (die strukturell nahe 100% liegt)'
dimensions.criterion: Repeat/paraphrase agreement rate not substantially worse than Variant A's (structurally near 100%, since A is deterministic and BLS-only with no source of run-to-run variance); qualitative, no fixed multiplier.
dimensions.v3042FidelityDefect: Verdict resolved to 'passed' purely from overlayGroupCount >= 1, never consulting the already-computed real agreement rates.
dimensions.developmentEvidence: Not partition-split (computed once over all 16 frozen overlay groups combined). See combined evidence.
dimensions.combinedEvidence: overlayGroupCount=16, variantBOutcomeAgreementRate=62.5%, variantBIdentificationAgreementRate=62.5%, variantCOutcomeAgreementRate=68.75%, variantCIdentificationAgreementRate=68.75%, variantCFastPathDeterministicConsistencyRate=100%, variantAStructuralBaselineRate=100% (structural, not separately measured), variantCOutcomeAgreementDeltaFromBaseline=-31.25pp, variantCIdentificationAgreementDeltaFromBaseline=-31.25pp.
dimensions.humanJudgment: A 31.25-percentage-point gap between Variant C's real repeat agreement (68.75%) and Variant A's structural ~100% baseline is a substantial, non-trivial degradation -- roughly one in three semantically-identical repeated/paraphrased log entries would be classified differently on repetition. In my judgment this qualifies as 'wesentlich schlechter' (substantially worse) than the baseline and does not meet the qualitative bar the spec intends, representing a real user-facing consistency problem.
dimensions.confidence: moderate -- n=16 overlay groups is a small sample for a percentage-point estimate; Variant B's own agreement (62.5%) is also mediocre, suggesting part of the gap may reflect corpus/ground-truth ambiguity rather than being attributable to Variant C alone, which tempers but does not reverse the adverse judgment
dimensions.unresolvedLimitations: Small n=16 overlay-group sample; metric is not partition-split; attribution between corpus-level ambiguity and model-level inconsistency is not fully separable from this evidence alone.
dimensions.productionConsequence: Formally requires_human_judgment (not a hard failure literal), but the substantive judgment above is adverse and is treated as not fulfilled for purposes of the 'all dimensions must be fulfilled' gate rule.

reliabilityAndTerminalFailureImplication.note: 8 of the 16 terminal failures returned HTTP 200 with billed usage but were still classified network_error at the parse/interpretation layer, not the transport layer -- an error-taxonomy defect distinct from the G2 gate dimensions, feeding RESOLVER-V3-046's scope. A 6.08% terminal-failure rate is itself a production-readiness concern independent of the seven named gate dimensions.

overallGateRule.bindingAuthority: docs/domains/ZERA_FOOD_RESOLUTION_BENCHMARK_SPEC_1.md sec.11, gate table row G2: 'Kombinierte Dimensionen (alle muessen erfuellt sein)'
overallGateRule.rule: All seven G2 sub-dimensions (a-g) must be fulfilled (i.e. resolve to an affirmative 'passed') for G2 to pass. A dimension resolving to failed, not_evaluable, indeterminate, or an adverse requires_human_judgment is not fulfilled. No dimension is averaged against another; a single unfulfilled mandatory dimension is sufficient to fail G2.
overallGateRule.effectOfOneFailedDimension: fails G2 overall, independent of all other dimensions
overallGateRule.effectOfNotEvaluableOrIndeterminate: counts as not fulfilled; never defaults to a pass

rationale: Two dimensions fail under deterministic, predeclared, hard/binding criteria computed directly from byte-verified frozen evidence: G2-B (false confidence -- Development Variant C rate 6.48% is not strictly below Variant A's 5.00%, violating the hard, non-averageable 'strictly lower than both A and B' criterion) and G2-D (latency -- Holdout AI-routed p95 12417.52ms exceeds the predeclared 12000ms ceiling, and Holdout all-attempts p95 12428.31ms does likewise, violating the one-violation, per-partition-independent rule). Under the binding 'all dimensions must be fulfilled' rule, either failure alone is sufficient to fail G2 overall; both are present. Independently, G2-A is indeterminate at the category level (V3-042 finding), G2-C and G2-G resolve to requires_human_judgment with this task's own explicit adverse judgment on both (poor abstention correctness ~4.65%/5.88%; a real -31.25pp consistency gap), and G2-E remains not_evaluable. Only G2-F (provenance) is affirmatively fulfilled. This verdict is decidable, not indeterminate, because G2-B and G2-D rest on deterministic evidence and predeclared, non-post-hoc thresholds that require no qualitative judgment to apply.
resolverV3010Rationale: RESOLVER-V3-010's dependency on a passed representative Hybrid gate is not satisfied by this re-decision (formal verdict RESOLVER_V3_G2_NOT_PASSED). Its ROADMAP.md dependency list is updated to add RESOLVER-V3-041 and RESOLVER-V3-048; it may only become unblocked once a future task (RESOLVER-V3-048) produces new, complete, Haiku-only live evidence that genuinely passes every mandatory G2 dimension under this same binding rule.

noProductionEffectStatement: This task made zero Anthropic/provider calls, incurred zero additional benchmark cost, reran neither Development nor Holdout, and changed no BLS data, alias, lookup, parser, routing, prompt, provider, or feature-flag code. Its only repository effects are this report, its JSON companion, ROADMAP.md, and handoffs/latest-handoff.md. All seven RESOLVER-V3-039 evidence files remain byte-identical to their PR #168-merged content.
